symptom: `DROP LAYOUT Mod.Name` is a parse error. Layouts are the only doctype mxcli can create and alter but not delete, so a layout authored wrongly — including one mxcli itself just wrote — cannot be removed headlessly.
cause: Pure wiring gap. `DeleteLayout` existed and worked on BOTH engines and is exercised on every CREATE OR REPLACE LAYOUT (the replace half is a delete + create); only the grammar alternative, AST node, visitor branch and executor were missing.
fix: dropStatement alternative + ast.DropLayoutStmt + visitor branch + mdl/executor/cmd_layouts_drop.go, plus the stmt_summary and validate_duplicates switches. Pages still bound are named in a warning, not refused.
insight: Before designing a 'missing capability', check whether the backend already has it — here the delete was already on the write path, so the whole feature was four small wirings and the risk was near zero. The second question is what the DROP's dependency policy should be: mxcli has NO drop that refuses on dependents, and warn-not-refuse is also what makes drop-then-recreate work (pages rebind by qualified name — verified back to 0 errors). The warning is load-bearing because the consequence, CE1613, names the PAGE and never the layout that was removed.
controls: Dropping a layout one page used → 2× CE1613 naming the page; re-creating it under the same name → 0 errors. A page bound to a DIFFERENT layout must not appear in the warning, and an unused layout must produce no warning at all.
